selection_criteria: Leadership quality - passionate and dynamic individuals spearheading successful work who would benefit from the funding and profile a Whitley Award provides and can use the visibility to scale up their work
Teamwork - a single named project leader supported by a strong team and/or local NGO with strong conservation experience, excellent ambassadorship, and members local to the country or region

Scientific foundation - professional scientific qualifications are not required, but projects addressing issues on a biological level must demonstrate activities informed by robust scientific evidence
Mid-career - an established track record with experience in managing grants at a similar scale to a Whitley Award, poised to scale up; defined by experience rather than age
Ecosystem level approach over purely single-species focus, with measurable biodiversity conservation impact
Community involvement - projects that actively involve and genuinely engage the community, bringing tangible benefits and strengthening capacity
Evidence of prior success - a track record of success relevant to the proposed activities, with appropriate metrics and baseline data
Pragmatic, replicable and scalable - practical grassroots initiatives given priority over purely scientific or academic activities; pilot or start-up projects are not funded
Measurable outcomes - clear indicators that evidence impact, e.g. how change in behaviour or anti-poaching effectiveness will be measured
Cost-effectiveness - value for money, with no high percentage of the Award spent on salaries and international travel
Demonstrate need - WFN funding should form a significant component (e.g. at least 30%) of the project's financial requirement
Sustainability - evidence the project can become self-supporting or able to levy further funds over time, and can continue should the team leader move on
Ability to manage funds appropriately, as demonstrated by historical financial documents and audited accounts

official.application_route: No nomination needed - register for a WFN account at wfn.eformsolutions.com, complete the online form, upload the current-year Word logframe and Excel budget templates, and nominate three referees who submit references through the portal.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be nationals of the country where they work (born there, or having lived there long term and obtained national status); non-nationals may only contact WFN in exceptional cases based on long-term residency (15+ years) and demonstrable commitment; expatriates are not funded.
official.international_eligibility: Open to nationals of any eligible country (those not classified as High-Income Economies by the World Bank, with WFN exceptions) - the award is for local leaders rather than international students.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Applicants must work for or have a formal agreement with a locally incorporated registered charity, NGO, not-for-profit or university; government employees are not funded, though staff at government-funded universities are typically eligible.
official.research_requirement: Pure academic research is not funded - winners must have objectives beyond research and publication, and any research should be applied research; MSc or PhD fieldwork is excluded.
official.duration: Each Whitley Award is worth GBP 50,000 in project funding to be spent over a one-year period; winners are announced at the annual Whitley Awards Ceremony in London in Spring 2027.
official.description: Awarded annually by the Whitley Fund for Nature and presented by WFN's Patron HRH The Princess Royal, the Whitley Awards recognise grassroots conservation leaders, providing funding to support and scale up proven, science-based solutions that deliver lasting impact for both people and nature.
official.english_requirement: Applicants must be able to communicate in English. Total fluency is not required, but applicants must be able to communicate verbally in English without a translator, so that winners can take part fully in the Whitley Awards week involving interviews, networking events, training and media opportunities.

applicant_utility.summary: If you are a mid-career conservationist who is a national of the country where you work, you can apply directly - no invitation or nomination is needed - for GBP 50,000 of project funding that must be spent within one year. Everything runs through WFN's online portal: register an account, complete the form online (saving as you go), and upload this year's Word logframe and Excel budget templates before 23:59 GMT on 30 October 2026. Your three referees must submit their references through the same portal by that same moment, so brief them early. The money is project funding paid to your organisation, not a personal stipend or tuition support, so your organisation's finances and governance need to be in order to receive and manage it.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career, locally embedded national conservation leaders running a proven, science-based, community-engaged project for a locally incorporated NGO, charity, not-for-profit or university, with a track record and a team ready to scale up.
application_readiness_checklist: Verify your country appears on WFN's published eligible-countries list for the 2027 round before drafting anything - if it is absent you are not eligible this cycle.
Get your organisation's paperwork ready now: registration certificate, founding documents, and last year's audited accounts converted to GBP with the exchange rate and date stated.
Register on the portal early and download only the current 2027 Word and Excel templates - work from last year's files and your application will not be considered.
Brief your three referees at least a month ahead: at least one must be international, none may have a financial interest, and all must know your work well enough to comment with authority.
Build your budget so that a high share does not go on salaries and international travel, and show WFN funding forming at least around 30% of total project costs.
common_rejection_risks: Submitting on out-of-date templates from a previous year - WFN states these will not be considered.
One of the three referee references missing at the deadline - collecting them is the applicant's responsibility.
Presenting the work as a pilot or start-up project without prior results, baseline data and metrics.
Allocating a high percentage of the award to salaries and international travel, which WFN penalises in its cost-effectiveness screening.
WFN funding forming too small a share of the overall project budget - WFN is not designed to make minor contributions to very large projects.
Relying heavily on AI-generated application text - WFN screens for authenticity and says such applications are unlikely to be funded.
Applying as a team, joint entry, or on behalf of someone else - only single named project leaders are eligible.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The GBP 50,000 must fund the project itself; WFN does not publish it as covering the applicant's living costs, tuition, or fees, and the remaining project costs beyond the award must be met from other sources. Personal travel, visas and accommodation for the London awards week are not stated to be covered by the award.
document_audit: Audited accounts must include an income and expenditure statement, a balance sheet, and an audit report signed by an independent external auditor - audit is preferred but not required, but the documents must be complete.
Values in financial statements must be converted to GBP with the exchange rate and date used stated on the document.
Applications from India additionally need an FCRA registration number.
The logframe must evidence measurable impact with well-considered indicators - stating activity counts (e.g. 'train 200 people') is not enough without showing what change will be measured.
Founding documents and audit statements should carry an English translation where available.
alerts: The deadline is a hard cut-off: 23:59 GMT on 30 October 2026, and referee references are due by the same moment - no extensions or email applications.
Templates are updated annually and applications on previous-year forms are rejected outright.
Re-applicants are rejected twice may not apply for a third consecutive year, and any re-application needs three new reference statements.
Only individuals apply - teams, joint entries and nominations on someone else's behalf are ineligible.
There is no appeals process; the Judging Panel's decision is final and WFN does not enter correspondence about unsuccessful applications.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on the WFN portal, complete and regularly save the online form, upload the current-year Word logframe and Excel budget, then ensure all three referees submit their references via the portal before the deadline - nothing is accepted by email.
